items.title: Conditions for a Proposition to be Satisfiable

source_refs.note: Unnumbered heading Conditions for a Proposition to be Satisfiable under 2.7, as printed (PDF 30, printed 26).

blocks.text: A proposition is satisfiable if there is at least one combination of truth values that makes it true. If all possible combinations make it false, it is unsatisfiable. Satisfiability depends on the structure of the expression and the logical connectives used. Logical connectives like AND, OR, and NOT determine whether a statement can be true. Checking all possible cases using a truth table is one way to test satisfiability. A proposition with at least one “true” outcome is satisfiable. This condition helps in reasoning and decision-making.
